T2 (round 2): a leased loop's period is now floor(due / period) on the ticking process's own clock, not the database's clock less the time since due, which the tester showed still lets a stall after the measure move a tick into the next period. The cost, written in exclusive.go's readPeriod comment and measured against Postgres in round 3: while two processes run, an offset between their clocks costs at most one extra pass (one 300 ms behind: six passes over five periods, then only the other); once the process whose clock runs ahead stops, the other skips one whole period's pass with a chance of about offset/period, so two passes stand up to two periods apart, once; a clock stepped back by X skips at most ceil(X / period) ticks.
